claims.claim: Recurring default names ('Marcus Webb', 'Sarah Chen') and the number 47 appear across unrelated AI stories, alongside canon-breaking facts.
A character shifts from heated argument to gentleness with no organic transition.
Words like 'fluorescent', 'humming', 'particular' recur at rates traceable to a specific model's slop profile.
Literary agents receive near-identical AI query letters with the same voice, language and content even when the manuscripts look human.
claims.quote: almost identical query letters that used the same voice

claims.claim: An agent found the AI query offered no hook, fabricated a comp she never represented, and read as real-but-fake.
claims.quote: it appears real but it isn't

claims.feature: worse than a worst first draft
claims.claim: Larian's writing director rates generated dialogue 3/10 at best, below his own worst drafts, and says placeholder AI text does not help development.
claims.source: Adam Smith (Larian) via PC Gamer, Ted Litchfield
claims.quote: the results hit a 3/10 at best

claims.claim: Generated text across Grok, Claude and ChatGPT carries a recognizable smarmy, sycophantic tone that editing cannot remove cheaply.
claims.quote: a by turns smarmy and sycophantic tone

claims.claim: LLM NPCs pad trivial exchanges with unnecessary words and nonsensical attributes (eighteen as 'a heavy, beautiful number').
claims.quote: filling up space with completely unnecessary words

claims.claim: AI NPCs rephrase plain questions into stilted 'alive-sounding' forms, which reads as trying too hard.
claims.quote: How many years have you lived?

claims.claim: The same evaluative words ('heavy', 'beautiful', 'iconic', 'vibes') attach to age, names and shoe colour alike; conversations contain no actual meaning.
claims.quote: a full conversation that contains no actual meaning

claims.claim: The one thing that worked in Seed: creator-chosen personality types (curt vs gushing) read through the AI dialogue.
LLM NPCs in a Song-dynasty wuxia game discuss ketchup and accept fake pregnancies; players break canon at will.
claims.source: PC Gamer on Where Winds Meet
claims.quote: ketchup wasn't available during the Song dynasty

claims.claim: Nvidia's ACE demo NPC lines were structurally fine yet robotic, with no personality or charm.
An LLM NPC that forgets its faction or backstory, leaks modern facts into a fantasy setting, or spills quest secrets under manipulation is useless to a designer.
claims.source: Gameindustry.com, 'The Hard Problem of AI NPCs', 2026-05-18
claims.quote: forget their faction or personal backstory

claims.claim: Barks, journals and ambient NPC lines are the backbone of a game's sense of place; generic filler makes the whole world feel shallower.
claims.quote: disconnected, jilted, random stories to tell you
